_meta.title: Mars Tactical EVA Configuration & Model Constants
_meta.note: All scoring bounds, dataset provenance, SIM 3292 geologic unit suitabilities, and solar-cycle radiation factors are declared here with explicit sources.

radiusM.source: IAU/IAG Mars 2000 Sphere (USGS SIM 3292 & MOLA standard)

boxSizeKm.source: Design choice: 4 km x 4 km (16 km^2) local EVA grid

gridN.source: Design choice: 40 x 40 grid at 100 m/cell

cellSizeM.source: Design choice: 4000 m / 40 = 100 m per cell

globalBaselineDeliveredM.source: web/layers/meta.json: 4096x2048 global equirectangular grid (pi*3396190*2 / 4096 = 5209.2 m/px at equator)

globalMolaSampledM.source: web/layers/meta.json: MOLA 463 m source sampled to 9216x4608 (~2.3 km) before 4096x2048 cell averaging

globalTesDeliveredM.source: web/layers/meta.json: TES_Thermal_Inertia_numeric & TES_Dust_numeric fetched at 2048x1024 and upsampled 2x (~10.4 km/px)

localDemNativeM.source: USGS MOLA-HRSC Blended DEM Global v2 (Fergason, Hare & Laura 2018): 200 m/px native topography & slope

localThemisNativeM.source: ASU/USGS THEMIS Day IR Global Mosaic v12 (100 m/px) & 100 m THEMIS TI cutouts

defaultOrbitalWeight.source: Prompt default 50/50 blend between center user-condition base and local orbital data: blended(r,c) = (1 - w) * centerBase + w * localOrbital(r,c)

tauRange.source: MGS TES / MER / MSL observed atmospheric column visible optical depth tau (~0.2 clearest aphelion to 10.8 MY34 global dust storm peak)

tauPresets.label: Clear
tauPresets.source: Typical northern spring/summer clear background tau ~0.4-0.6 (Smith 2004 / Guzewich et al.)

tauPresets.label: Dusty season
tauPresets.source: Perihelion dusty season nominal regional haze tau ~1.5 (Ls ~180-330)

tauPresets.label: Regional storm
tauPresets.source: Major regional dust storm opacity tau ~3-5

tauPresets.label: 2018 global storm
tauPresets.source: NASA Opportunity / Curiosity MY34 (June 2018) planet-encircling dust storm peak tau ~10.8

radiation.baselineModelRef: SCORING.radDose (web/scoring.js, anchored to MSL/RAD Hassler et al. 2014 Science 343: 0.64 mSv/day = 233.6 mSv/yr at 0 km, Cycle-24 mid)

min.label: Solar min
min.source: Guo et al. (2015) / Matthia et al. (2016) / Hassler et al. (2014): Solar minimum GCR unshielded surface dose rate ~0.82-0.90 mSv/day (~1.33x Cycle-24 0.64 mSv/day baseline)

mid.label: Solar mid
mid.source: Hassler et al. (2014) Science 343: MSL/RAD surface measurement during Cycle-24 mid/declining phase (~0.64 +/- 0.12 mSv/day)

max.label: Solar max
max.source: Matthia et al. (2017) / Guo et al. (2018): Solar maximum heliospheric GCR modulation lowers surface dose rate to ~0.30-0.36 mSv/day (~0.52x Cycle-24 baseline)

doseBestMSvYr.source: Normalization lower bound near low-elevation Solar Max GCR floor (~80-110 mSv/yr -> score 100)

doseWorstMSvYr.source: Normalization upper bound near high-elevation Solar Min GCR (~360 mSv/yr -> score ~0 before SPE)

speAcutePenaltyDivisorMSv.source: Assumption: normalizes acute SCORING.calcSPE unshielded dose (300-500 mSv) into 0-100 score reduction when SPE toggle is ON

kGlobalMeanWtPct.source: Boynton et al. (2007) JGR 112 E12S99 (Mars Odyssey GRS 5x5 deg global average K ~0.32 wt%)

thGlobalMeanPpm.source: Boynton et al. (2007) JGR 112 E12S99 (Mars Odyssey GRS 5x5 deg global average Th ~0.59 ppm)

footprintKm.source: Boynton et al. (2007): GRS spatial resolution ~550 km FWHM binned at 5x5 deg; unreliable > +/-60 deg high-latitude H-diluted zones

tiWeight.source: Assumption: relative weight of soil firmness (TI) vs operating surface temperature

tempWeight.source: Assumption: relative weight of instantaneous diurnal surface temperature from STORM.surfaceTempC

tiFineDustM.source: Mellon et al. (2000) / Fergason et al. (2006): fine dust/loose drift TI < ~100 J m^-2 K^-1 s^-1/2

tiOptLow.source: Christensen (1986) / Mellon et al. (2000): cohesive duricrust / coarse sand-gravel mix (~250-500 tiu)

tiOptHigh.source: Optimal rover traction / regolith load-bearing window upper knee (~500 tiu)

tiRockUpper.source: Assumption: high-TI bedrock blockfield penalty knee (>500 up to 900+ tiu indicates exposed hard bedrock/boulders)

tempWarmOptC.source: Assumption: benign rover/actuator daytime thermal operating band near -10 C

tempColdFloorC.source: Viking/MSL thermal floor: near CO2 frost point -125 C imposes max cold thermal penalty

reliefMaxM.source: Assumption: 300 m neighborhood relief >= 45 m yields near-zero local relief score before speed risk

roughMaxM.source: Assumption: MOLA baseline roughness std-dev >= 25 m (scaled down when 100 m DEM available) maps to worst roughness score

reliefShare.source: Assumption: weight of 100-200 m DEM local 3x3 relief vs global MOLA roughness / CTX texture contrast

albedoIdealMin.source: Christensen et al. (2001): dark/intermediate basaltic-mixed surfaces (0.14-0.25 Lambert albedo; brighter >0.28 indicates thick dust mantle)

albedoIdealMax.source: Christensen et al. (2001): above ~0.25-0.30 corresponds to high-albedo dust-mantled regions (e.g. Tharsis/Arabia)

albedoHighDust.source: Assumption: high bright-dust albedo bound reducing trafficability/rock exposure contrast

tauVisibilityScale.source: Assumption: Beer-Lambert optical navigation / stereo-camera haze visibility attenuation exp(-tau / 4.0)

nightSolarZenithPenalty.source: Assumption: low solar elevation / night-time LTST reduces optical camera visibility factor via solarZenithCos

elevShare.source: Assumption: 30% weight on existing SCORING.F.elev rule (lower = thicker air), 70% weight on traversable slope margin & mass sinkage

slopeShare.source: Assumption: primary weighting of slope headroom against active vehicle slopeLimitDeg (zero score if slope > limit)

dciClean.source: Ruff & Christensen (2002) JGR 107(E12): TES Dust Cover Index >= 0.96-0.98 indicates nearly dust-free bedrock/sand

dciDusty.source: Ruff & Christensen (2002): TES DCI <= 0.90 indicates optically thick surface dust cover

surfaceDciShare.source: Assumption: equal split between archival surface dust cover index (DCI) and active atmospheric optical depth tau

baseFineCutout.source: Assumption: base confidence for 100 m THEMIS + 200 m MOLA-HRSC local cutout

hiriseBoost.source: Assumption: additional confidence boost where 1 m USGS HiRISE DTM coverage is present

baseGlobalFallback.source: Assumption: reduced confidence when offline custom coordinates rely on ~5.2 km/px global rasters

tauUncertaintyPenalty.source: Assumption: maximum optical/thermal retrieval uncertainty penalty under tau -> 10.8 storm dust load

geologyFallbackScore.source: Assumption: neutral prior suitability when a custom polygon unit is outside known lookup keys

fieldBoostMax.source: Assumption: confidence uplift when in-situ field measurements cover a cell

vetoCapScore.source: Design choice: when daily generated energy < daily demand (deficit), power score = 0 and final score is vetoed <= 20

comfortableReserveRatio.source: Assumption: generation/demand >= 2.0x maps to Power & Energy score 100; 1.0x break-even maps to score 50

solarDustFloorScore.source: Assumption: minimum power score before total deficit veto when solar survival reserve margin is near 1.0x

activeDutyHoursPerSol.source: Assumption: nominal daily active EVA/drive operations + 0.15x sleep standby hotel duty over 24.66 h sol (solar arrays sleep overnight)

sleepHotelFraction.source: Assumption: low-power avionics sleep standby fraction outside active drive window (radiisotope/nuclear runs continuous 24h thermal/bus bus)

nuclearWasteHeatOffset.source: Assumption: MMRTG ~1900 W thermal waste heat covers 75% of cold trace-heating demand, leaving 25% electrical heater overhead in extreme cold

defaultInfluenceRadiusM.source: Design choice: default in-situ point influence radius = 300 m, adjustable in Advanced

discrepancyRelThreshold.source: Design choice: >50% relative difference between field measurement and orbital value triggers popup discrepancy warning

hazardSoftSandPenalty.source: Design choice: soft sand hazard marker reduces cell traversability (elevSlope & thermal sinkage)

hazardRockPenalty.source: Design choice: rock hazard marker reduces cell traversability (topography & elevSlope)

hazardCraterRimPenalty.source: Design choice: crater rim hazard marker reduces cell traversability

elevMaxM.source: Existing web/scoring.js SCORING.HARD.elevMax (NASA HLS-2015 MOLA <= +2.0 km landing elevation constraint)

absLatMaxDeg.source: Existing web/scoring.js SCORING.HARD.latMax (NASA HLS-2015 |lat| <= 50 deg latitude band)

slopeMaxDeg.source: Existing web/scoring.js SCORING.HARD.slopeMax (NASA HLS-2015 landing footprint slope <= 15 deg)

geologySim3292.citation: Tanaka, K.L., Skinner, J.A., Jr., Dohm, J.M., Irwin, R.P., III, Kolb, E.J., Fortezzo, C.M., Platz, T., Michael, G.G., & Hare, T.M. (2014). Geologic Map of Mars, 1:20,000,000. USGS SIM 3292.

lHl.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): broad planar sediment/flood-plain lowland favorable for mobility

eHb.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): smooth basin fill with fluvial/lacustrine plains potential

lHb.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): flat basin deposits favorable for wheeled traverses

eAb.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): lowland basin fill, low relief

HNb.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): ancient basin fill with high mineralogic interest & subdued relief

HNt.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): highland/lowland boundary knobs, mesas & plains (Jezero/Syrtis margins)

Htu.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): layered yardang/sedimentary plateaus with sulfate alteration

lHt.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): late transition deposits & dissected plateaus

Hto.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): outflow channel bar/scour terrain (locally streamlined/bouldery)

AHtu.desc: Amazonian and Hesperian transition undivided unit
AHtu.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): mantled knobby aprons along dichotomy boundary

lAv.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): planar flood lavas; competent substrate but platy/ridged textures locally

AHv.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): lava sheet flows with local roughness

lNh.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): cratered/dissected highlands with valley networks

mNh.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): uneven rolling cratered highlands (Nili Fossae basement); moderate local relief

eNh.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): ancient degraded highland crustal terrain

HNhu.desc: Hesperian and Noachian highland undivided unit

Aa.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): debris aprons & piedmont talus near scarps

lAa.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): blocky glacis / talus aprons around domes & scarps

ANa.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): slope-wash aprons and mass-wasted talus

AHi.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): impact crater ejecta, terraced walls & central peaks (blocky/hummocky)

mNhm.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): steep high-relief basin rim massifs

Nve.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): eroded volcanic shield edifices (steep flank slopes)

Hp.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): high-latitude polar terrain (extreme cold, low solar)

Apu.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): polar layered deposits & scarp troughs

lApd.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): polar erg sand dunes (high wheel sinkage risk)

lApc.source: Assumption (SIM 3292): perennial CO2/H2O polar ice cap (unsuited to baseline wheeled EVA)
